title: Evidence for Chapter 32: Keynes's General Theory, 1929-1937
source: Keynes, The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money (1936); Keynes, Essays in Persuasion (1931: 'Saving and Spending', broadcast January 1931; 'A Programme of Expansion', May 1929, with H. D. Henderson); Hansard (Commons, 15 April 1929 and 4 November 1936); the Macmillan Committee's Minutes of Evidence (1930); Kahn (1931); Pigou (1936); Ohlin (1937); Keynes (1937); Kalecki (1935); Mill (1844); Berg and Jonung (1998); Shizume (2009); Baumol (1999); Velde (2003); the authority records of the Library of Congress and the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the people pages of Historic Hansard
series: Evidence rows: id, place, year, values (';' separated, in the order of the quotation), unit, source key, page or column, the source text verbatim, note
license: Quotations for criticism, scholarship and teaching, each with its source; no full original is redistributed. Keynes (1883-1946): The General Theory (London: Macmillan, 1936; 'COPYRIGHT', row gt_copyright), Essays in Persuasion (1931; row ep_copyright) and 'Alternative Theories of the Rate of Interest' (1937) are in the public domain in the United Kingdom; the General Theory of 1936 may still be in copyright in the United States, so the chapter quotes it a sentence or less at a time and names the copy used. Kahn (1931), Pigou (1936), Ohlin (1937) and Kalecki (1935; Econometrica: 'Copyright 1935 by the Econometric Society.', row kc_copyright) are in copyright: the chapter quotes short phrases only and paraphrases the rest; the snapshot keeps the sentences needed to check those phrases and the figures of Kahn's table. Hansard (the Commons debates of 15 April 1929 and 4 November 1936 and the people pages): 'Contains Parliamentary information licensed under the Open Parliament Licence v3.0.' The people pages: '© UK Parliament'. The Macmillan Committee's Minutes of Evidence (HMSO, 1931) is a Crown publication older than fifty years and out of Crown copyright. Bank of Japan (Shizume 2009): the Bank's terms (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/copyright.htm): 'The information included in the site may be copied or reproduced with the exceptions below. When copying or reproducing, the source, the Bank of Japan, should be explicitly credited.' Berg and Jonung (1998), SSE/EFI working paper: no copyright notice found; short sentences only, with credit. Baumol (1999): one phrase of the abstract on the American Economic Association's article page. Velde (2003), Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago working paper: one sentence, paraphrased in the chapter. Mill (1844) is in the public domain; the Project Gutenberg text is used under the Project Gutenberg licence (no Project Gutenberg trademark is used here). The authority records of the Library of Congress (id.loc.gov) are public data; those of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (data.bnf.fr) are metadata reused under the Licence Ouverte (Open License). The chapter's Chinese renders the quotations; the translations are the book's.
citation: See the 'source' field; each row names its source key in the 'sources' object.
notes: Every quotation is checked word for word against the cached source text by data/fetch/verify_web_quotes.py, and every value is read from its quotation by checks/check_ch32.py; rows with an empty quotation are values or words read on a page image (sources keynes1936img, keynes1929cimg, kahn1931img), named as such in their notes, which give a transcription between « and ». The OCR texts keep their misreadings as printed and the notes name them: the line-end hyphen printed as '¬' in Essays in Persuasion ('un¬ luckily', 'sur¬ plus', 'adver¬ tised', 'per¬ spective', 're¬ duction', 'In¬ flation', 'deflation¬ ary', 'in¬ dustrial'), 'Listener^', '4-' (keynes1931b, keynes1929c); 'Jostan' (macmillan1930); 'Kaun' and the printed 'cf' (kahn1931); 'Picou' (pigou1936); 'Kreynzs' (keynes1937); 'Katecki' and 'Macrodynemic' (kalecki1935); '2-5' for 2·5 (keynes1936). The normalisation of verify_web_quotes.py joins a word broken by a hyphen at a line end, so two quotations of the General Theory read 'liquiditypreferences' and 'investmentdemand'. Indirect testimony: Churchill's Budget speech as Keynes and Henderson quote it ('dogma', row pe_dogma; Hansard prints 'doctrine', row hc29_doctrine); Cunningham's history through the Budget speech (row hc29_crisis); Kuznets's estimates through the General Theory (rows gt_kuz_*; NBER Bulletin 52 was not obtained); the Swedish Unemployment Committee's reports through Ohlin (1937); Myrdal's report for the budget of 1933 through Berg and Jonung (row bj_myrdal); the praise of Takahashi as a pioneer of Keynesian economics through Shizume (row sz_pioneer); Pigou's reading of Keynes's long-period conclusion (row pg_longperiod); the Prime Minister's reply of 29 October 1936 through Runciman (row hc36b_improved); the words of the Jarrow petition are the petitioners', presented by Ellen Wilkinson.
